name: SBA Microloan Program
description: The SBA Microloan Program provides small loans up to $50,000 to help small businesses and certain not-for-profit childcare centers start up and expand. The average microloan is about $13,000. Loans are delivered through nonprofit community-based intermediary lenders, which also provide business training and technical assistance. The program is particularly valuable for immigrant entrepreneurs who may lack traditional credit history or collateral, as intermediary lenders use flexible underwriting criteria. Microloans can be used for working capital, inventory, supplies, furniture, fixtures, machinery, and equipment. The maximum repayment term is six years.
eligibility: Small businesses and certain nonprofit childcare centers; available to all legal residents including immigrants with work authorization; no minimum credit score required by SBA (intermediary lenders set individual criteria)
applicationProcess: Contact an SBA-approved intermediary lender in your area through the SBA Lender Match tool at sba.gov; intermediaries provide both loan funding and required business training
geographicScope: National (SBA-approved intermediary lenders in all 50 states)
documentsRequired: Business plan, financial statements, personal identification, proof of work authorization; specific requirements vary by intermediary lender

name: Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) Business Centers
organization: U.S. Department of Commerce — Minority Business Development Agency
description: The Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) is the only federal agency dedicated to the growth and global competitiveness of minority-owned businesses in the United States. MBDA operates a nationwide network of business centers that provide strategic business consulting, access to capital, access to contracts, and market development services. Centers help minority and immigrant entrepreneurs connect with banks, investors, venture capital, and federal contracting opportunities. MBDA programs support a total package valued at over $500 billion per year in federal grants and business initiatives. Services include financial readiness assessments, loan packaging, bonding assistance, and mentorship programs.
eligibility: Minority-owned businesses including those owned by immigrants; minorities defined as African American, Asian, Hasidic Jewish, Hispanic, Native American, and Pacific Islander business owners
amount: Free business consulting and access to capital networks; individual funding amounts vary by program
applicationProcess: Contact the nearest MBDA Business Center for an initial consultation; centers are located across the country and provide customized assistance based on business needs
geographicScope: National (business centers in major metropolitan areas across the U.S.)
documentsRequired: Business registration documents, financial statements, identification; requirements vary by specific program and service

name: Microenterprise Development (MED) Program
organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)
description: The Microenterprise Development (MED) Program, administered by the Office of Refugee Resettlement, provides grants to organizations that help refugees develop, expand, or sustain microenterprise businesses in the United States. The program funds business training, technical assistance, microloans, revolving lines of credit, and individual development accounts (IDAs) specifically for refugee entrepreneurs. MED grants support refugees in achieving economic self-sufficiency through self-employment and small business ownership. Organizations receiving MED grants typically offer culturally and linguistically appropriate services including business plan development, financial literacy, marketing assistance, and mentorship from established business owners.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders, victims of trafficking, and other ORR-eligible populations in the United States
amount: Varies; microloans typically $500–$15,000; IDA matching funds also available
applicationProcess: Refugees access services through ORR-funded local resettlement agencies and microenterprise development organizations; organizations apply for MED grants through annual ORR funding announcements
geographicScope: National (services provided through local ORR-funded organizations in states with significant refugee populations)
documentsRequired: Proof of ORR-eligible immigration status, business concept or plan, identification documents; specific requirements vary by local program

name: Canada Start-up Visa Program
description: The Canada Start-up Visa Program is an immigration pathway that gives immigrant entrepreneurs permanent residency in Canada by linking them with Canadian private sector organizations that have experience in working with start-ups. Unlike most startup visa programs worldwide, Canada's program offers immediate permanent residency upon qualification rather than temporary status. The program connects entrepreneurs with designated venture capital funds, angel investor groups, and business incubators who can provide funding, mentorship, and business guidance. Canada issues up to 1,000 startup visas per year, making it one of the most generous entrepreneur immigration programs globally. Applicants must receive a commitment from a designated organization and meet language and settlement fund requirements.
eligibility: International entrepreneurs with a qualifying business concept; must obtain a letter of support from a designated organization (venture capital fund commitment of $200,000+, angel investor group commitment of $75,000+, or acceptance into a designated business incubator)
amount: Minimum investment from designated organization: $200,000 (VC fund) or $75,000 (angel investor group); incubator acceptance has no minimum investment
applicationProcess: Pitch your business to a designated organization (listed on IRCC website); if accepted, receive a letter of support; submit permanent residency application to IRCC with letter of support, language test results, and proof of settlement funds
geographicScope: National (Canada-wide; designated organizations located across provinces)
documentsRequired: Letter of support from designated organization, language test results (CLB 5 minimum), proof of settlement funds, business ownership documentation, police certificates, medical examination

name: EXIST Business Startup Grant (Existenzgründungen aus der Wissenschaft)
organization: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK)
description: The EXIST Business Startup Grant is a support program from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action that provides funding for students, graduates, and scientists from German universities and research institutions to prepare innovative technology-based or knowledge-based startup projects. The program is explicitly open to international students and researchers at German institutions. Funding covers living expenses for up to one year (up to EUR 3,000/month for PhD holders, EUR 2,500/month for graduates, EUR 1,000/month for students), plus up to EUR 10,000 for materials and EUR 5,000 for coaching. The grant is non-repayable and specifically designed to bridge the gap between academic research and business startup.
eligibility: Students, graduates (up to 5 years after graduation), and scientists at German universities and research institutions; open to international students and researchers; teams of up to 3 people
amount: Up to EUR 3,000/month (PhD), EUR 2,500/month (graduates), EUR 1,000/month (students) for 12 months; plus EUR 10,000 materials + EUR 5,000 coaching
applicationProcess: Apply through your German university's EXIST contact point or technology transfer office; university submits the application to the EXIST program office (Project Management Agency Jülich) on behalf of the founding team
geographicScope: Germany (all German universities and research institutions)
documentsRequired: Business plan, team qualifications, university endorsement letter, technology/innovation description, market analysis, financial plan

name: Amber Grant for Women Entrepreneurs
description: The Amber Grant is a monthly and annual business grant program for women entrepreneurs in the United States, founded in 1998 in honor of a young woman named Amber who died before realizing her entrepreneurial dreams. WomensNet awards $10,000 every month to a woman-owned business, and at the end of each year, one monthly winner receives an additional $25,000 annual grant. The program also offers a $10,000 monthly Startup Grant for businesses less than two years old. The Amber Grant is open to all women business owners including immigrants, regardless of immigration status, race, or industry. The application process is simple with a $15 fee, and thousands of women apply each month making it one of the most accessible recurring grant programs for women entrepreneurs.
eligibility: Women business owners in the United States; open to all industries, business stages, and backgrounds including immigrant women entrepreneurs
amount: $10,000 monthly grant; $25,000 annual grant to one monthly winner; separate $10,000 monthly Startup Grant
applicationProcess: Submit online application at ambergrantsforwomen.com with $15 application fee; describe your business and how the grant would help; monthly winners announced on the website
documentsRequired: Online application form, business description, explanation of how funds will be used; $15 application fee

name: UK Innovator Founder Visa
organization: UK Home Office — UK Visas and Immigration
description: The UK Innovator Founder Visa is an immigration route for experienced entrepreneurs who want to set up or run an innovative business in the United Kingdom. The visa replaced the former Innovator visa in April 2023 and is specifically designed for international entrepreneurs bringing new business ideas to the UK market. Applicants must be endorsed by an approved body that assesses the business idea for innovation, viability, and scalability. The visa is granted for an initial three years and can lead to settlement (permanent residency) after three years if the business meets key performance indicators. There is no minimum investment requirement under the new route, though applicants must demonstrate they have sufficient funds to support themselves and grow the business.
eligibility: International entrepreneurs with an innovative, viable, and scalable business idea; must be endorsed by an approved endorsing body; English language requirement (CEFR Level B2); must have maintenance funds of at least GBP 1,270
amount: No minimum investment requirement; maintenance funds of GBP 1,270 required; some endorsing bodies offer startup competitions with prizes of GBP 15,000–60,000
applicationProcess: Contact an approved endorsing body (listed on gov.uk) to pitch your business idea; if endorsed, apply for the visa online through the UK government website; attend a biometric appointment
geographicScope: United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland)
documentsRequired: Endorsement letter from approved body, proof of English language ability, proof of maintenance funds, valid passport, tuberculosis test results (if applicable), criminal record certificate
